wholeLooks.rule: twelve approved palette/style cards whose light and dark versions are both available, six score leaders with distinct colour families and styles, followed by six contrasts from look 1 (including either). Score ties retain library order. Choose contrasts slot by slot, in order, keeping the cards already chosen. At each slot, change exactly one aggregate position whenever a one-dial card can complete the page from that prefix meeting every rule; only when no such one-dial card can complete it may the slot change exactly two. Every contrast differs from look 1. A palette id ends in -muted, -balanced or -bold; its prefix is its colour family. A style fixes the pairing, graphic set and container. Prefer an unused contrast dial, then an unused destination on that dial, then a family not yet on the page, then score and library order. Palettes never repeat; no family/style pair repeats, no style appears more than twice, and no colour family appears more than twice, across leaders and contrasts alike. At least two cards have plain-ground styles C, E or J, and all five marks appear: seal, badge, letter, stack and initials. Each card keeps its style's background and its mode's approved depth, with cardDepth fields replacing the style's fields whole; no slot changes pattern strength. One primary mode covers the page, in this order: kept.primaryMode; light when off names darkLed; dark for a dark mode tap not dropped by off; light for a light mode tap not dropped by off; otherwise (Either, skipped or dropped) dark when darkLed is above zero, else light. A whole look's six positions are the unweighted majority of its pairing, palette and graphic set; either contributes zero. The checked greedy pass falls back to a feasibility search when it cannot complete a page with every rule intact. The first page is shown once. With nothing picked, "None of these work" brings the three this-or-that taps and fourth "What's missing from these?" question on the question tool, with Nothing to add as its only option and the tool's typed answer taking a comment, then twelve unshown looks from another angle on the same card. The session reads the comment into `steer` and `off`. Keep all looks shown in this sitting in `shown`; the member may ask again. Each new page favours families, palettes and styles not yet shown and keeps every page rule, refusing with `library exhausted` when no new page of twelve can be made. Every picked look adds one tick toward each of its non-either positions, so shared positions receive more weight. These ticks are selection steer, never adopted design rules.
